answer: An identity is paid only after a stranger, assigned at random and never twice the same pairing, actually builds on its work in a later job and that second job passes review. Like a marble slab cut by one hand, framed in timber by another, and set with onyx by a third, each piece must fit hands it never chose. A farm's clones can praise each other for free, but they cannot make outside builders risk their own standing on useless output, so every sybil must produce work real strangers can use, which removes the cheap multiplication.
